parallel.requirements: Recognized the 17 required Java experiment/homework modules, exact method signatures, and required per-slug non-empty patch plus commit workflow.

parallel.implementation: Implemented and committed dsexp01_stack and ds03_priorityqueue, using tracked bytecode/decompilation as a recovery path for priority queue.

parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Most required modules remained stubbed, including graph, search, red-black tree, hash, DS01, loser tree, farmer, project, and island lake paths.

serial.requirements: Received the same 17-module prompt and git workflow requirements, but did not perform repository survey or requirement analysis.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Serial mode disabled multi-agent execution and recorded zero spawn calls; no local work plan was produced before the failed turn.
serial.implementation: No source edits, patch files, commits, or tool calls were produced before the stream-disconnect failure.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The patch timeline stayed empty, so there was no implementation to integrate, package, or deliver.
serial.verification: No local checks were run by the agent; official tests evaluated the mostly initial stub state and reported 5 passed with 47 failed in the test pane.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The attempt ended at startup with unchanged TODO stubs across the assignment, including stack and priority queue failures that parallel later improved.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The prompt required all 17 Java data-structures modules and warned that partial fixes would fail; the parallel run read the requirement files and recognized the broad scope.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the same 17-module prompt, but the agent disconnected before doing any repository or requirement work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel converted the shared prompt into a survey and partial implementation plan, while serial never acted on the same requirements.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent explicitly split the survey across sub-agents and kept local implementation ownership for at least stack and priority queue work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control had multi-agent disabled, zero spawn calls, and no delegated work or local implementation actions before failure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created a multi-agent inspection plan with three children; serial had no decomposition beyond the single failed parent process.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent delegated targeted inspection scopes for search/RBT, graph/tree, and DS04 work, but the child task text is opaque and no usable technical handoff returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child brief, handoff, or cross-agent interface boundary because it never got past startup.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material context difference is not a bad interface contract; it is that parallel created child context boundaries whose outputs failed, whereas serial never created them.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented and committed dsexp01_stack and ds03_priorityqueue, including a successful priority-queue local run before committing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial made no requirement patches and official tests still saw the priority-queue TODO exception.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel materially improved two slugs relative to serial, but the implementation path still covered only a small subset of the 17 required modules.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All three inspection children reported task_complete with last_agent_message null and stream-disconnect errors, and the parent received error wrappers instead of usable results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle; its sole parent turn failed directly with the same stream-disconnect class of error.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a failed child-result lifecycle requiring takeover; serial had a startup failure with no delegated result to join or recover.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The retained workspace history shows only two requirement patch files and no evidence that child edits collided with parent edits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial patch timeline stayed empty, so there was no integration or shared-state activity to reconcile.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had limited integration of its own commits; neither mode shows a concrete multi-writer collision or artifact leakage event.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran focused local checks for the two implemented modules and official post-test results reported 14 passed and 38 failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no local checks before failure and official post-test output reported 5 passed and 47 failed in the initial-stub state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel performed some useful focused verification and improved the score, but neither run reached whole-task acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed a full multi-agent attempt, then the parent stream disconnected with implementation/testing TODOs still false.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial closed after an early stream disconnect, with zero LLM requests and zero tool calls recorded in status.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used the available window productively but incompletely; serial failed before consuming an implementation budget at all.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations failed. Parallel made more task progress, with two requirement patches and a 14-passed/38-failed post-test pane, while serial disconnected at startup and had no agent tool work or patches before a 5-passed/47-failed post-test pane. Because neither solution passed, the retained parallel coordination issue is an adverse process contributor to remaining failures, not an explanation for a discordant official outcome.
parallel_contributors: Parallel implemented and committed dsexp01_stack and ds03_priorityqueue, improving tests over the serial initial state.
Three delegated inspection scopes failed with no usable child result, and the parent did not take over those scopes before closure.
serial_contributors: Serial mode disabled delegation and the single parent turn stream-disconnected before any LLM/tool work was recorded.
Serial produced no requirement patch files or commits, so official tests ran against the initial stubbed code.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used tracked class files and local checks to recover two module implementations; serial made no implementation attempt.
Many remaining failures are ordinary unimplemented Java stubs rather than separately evidenced cross-agent write or interface conflicts.
evaluator_effects: The official pass/fail relation is taken from cell/status.json:evaluation; the status fields do not expose aggregate pass counts, so test-pane counts are used only for explanatory detail.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference: both failed; coordination evidence supports an adverse parallel process pattern but not a discordant-outcome root cause.

No separately produced child components reached integration, so there is no observable incompatible interface contract between agents.
